#+TITLE: ShowAllEntityData — Test Harness Guide
#+AUTHOR: generated by Claude Code
#+DATE: 2026-09-07

This is the practical guide to running ShowAllEntityData's Playwright test
harness: what the suites are, how to run them, and roughly how long each takes.

For *what to test and why*, see =CLAUDE.md='s "Testing expectations" section.
For *which pageTypes are covered and which are planned*, see
=PAGETYPES-TESTING-REFERENCE.org=. For *what each individual spec verifies*, see
=tests/live/registry.org= and =tests/snapshots/registry.org=.

* Quick start

#+begin_src sh
cd ShowAllEntityData
npm install          # first time only
npm test             # the safe default: 140 fixture tests, ~66 s, no network
#+end_src

=npm test= needs no network, no login, and no MusicBrainz cooperation. Start
there. Everything else in this file costs real time and real requests to
musicbrainz.org.

* The two suites

The harness is split into two Playwright projects, by directory.

| Project             | Directory         | Tests           | Network     | Per-test timeout |
|---------------------+-------------------+-----------------+-------------+------------------|
| =chromium-fixtures= | =tests/fixtures/= | 140 in 31 files | none        | 30 s (default)   |
| =chromium-live=     | =tests/live/=     | 71 in 37 files  | real MB.org | 120 s            |

*Fixtures* serve a saved local HTML file at a real musicbrainz.org-shaped URL
via Playwright's =page.route()=, so the userscript believes it is on the real
page while nothing leaves the machine. Deterministic and fast — this is where a
new test belongs unless it genuinely cannot be reproduced offline.

*Live* specs drive real musicbrainz.org pages. They are slower, occasionally
flaky through no fault of the code (MusicBrainz 503s under load, and the Cover
Art Archive serves at roughly 1.2 requests/second), and some are login-gated.

*A disk fixture is not the same thing as a fixture spec, and the difference
bites.* =loadFromDiskFixture()= (=tests/support/diskFixture.js=) restores a
saved =*.json.gz= payload through the real Load-from-disk pipeline, which makes
the TABLE DATA deterministic and free of MusicBrainz data drift. It does not
make the run offline *by itself*: called without =pageFixtureFile= it passes no
=fixtureFile= to =loadUserscriptPage()=, so no =page.route()= is registered and
the page SHELL is still fetched from the live site. Anything built that way —
=tests/live/artist-events-interactions.spec.js=, =capture-interaction-perf.js= —
therefore needs musicbrainz.org to be reachable, and belongs in =tests/live/=
for exactly that reason.

Pass =pageFixtureFile= (a saved raw shell, e.g.
=tests/snapshots/releasegroup-releases/raw.html=) to close that last gap and
make the whole disk-load path genuinely offline — then the spec belongs in
=tests/fixtures/=. =tests/fixtures/picard-cells-survive-rerender.spec.js= is
the worked example. The shell must be the same entity the =*.json.gz= was
captured from, or pageType detection and the hydrated rows disagree.

Two things that cost a run each when writing that spec, both about the *page*
rather than the data: the Load-from-disk dialog is a =position: fixed= overlay,
so when it is taller than the viewport its confirm button sits where no page
scrolling can reach it and Playwright retries "element is outside of the
viewport" until the hook times out — a raw shell has none of musicbrainz.org's
own CSS and so is taller than the live page, and the fix is a taller
spec-local =test.use({ viewport })=. And =releasegroup-releases= renders its
sub-sections COLLAPSED, so anything inside a sub-table is a 0×0 element until
=clickMasterToggleAndExpandAll()= has run.

Two complete 20-minute
perf runs were lost to a single 30 s navigation timeout while roughly one probe
in three to the host was timing out; =capture-interaction-perf.js= now retries a
failed sample rather than abandoning the run.

Note =fullyParallel: false= in =playwright.config.js=: tests *within* one file
run serially, but separate files still run in parallel across workers.
Playwright defaults to half the machine's cores.

** Live-spec tags

Every live spec carries exactly one tag, and the npm scripts select on it:

| Tag         | What it is                                                                                                             |
|-------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| =@core=     | Shared-mechanism sanity net — filter, sort, fetch, pagination basics                                                   |
| =@extended= | Bespoke / pageType-specific edge cases — Stop button, IDB cache tiers, third-party interop, sub-table filters, artwork |
| =@perf=     | The deliberate perf-comparison instrumentation only                                                                    |

Current split: =@core= 10 tests / 9 files · =@extended= 54 / 28 · =@perf= 7 / 1.

* Every npm script

| Command                                          | Runs                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------|
| =npm test=                                       | Fixtures only. The default and CI-safe suite. |
| =npm run test:live=                              | Live =@core= only                             |
| =npm run test:live:extended=                     | Live =@core= + =@extended= (64 tests)         |
| =npm run test:live:perf=                         | Live =@perf= only                             |
| =npm run test:all=                               | Literally everything, fixtures and live       |
| =npm run test:ui=                                | Playwright's interactive UI mode              |
| =npm run test:headed=                            | Same tests, visible browser                   |
| =npm run test:live:save-html=                    | Live suite, saving rendered HTML per test     |
| =npm run test:live:report:artist-releases=       | One spec + generates an =.org=/=.html= report |
| =npm run test:live:artist-releases:full=         | Same, with both opt-in test groups enabled    |
| =npm run test:live:report:releasegroup-releases= | Multi-table sibling of the above              |
| =npm run report=                                 | Open the last HTML report                     |
| =npm run auth:login=                             | One-time interactive MusicBrainz login        |
| =npm run live-interop=                           | Debugging aid, not a test — see below         |

To run a single spec directly:

#+begin_src sh
npx playwright test tests/fixtures/length-duration-sort.spec.js --project=chromium-fixtures
npx playwright test tests/live/smoke.spec.js --project=chromium-live
#+end_src

* How long things take

Two of these are *measured*; the rest are estimates or declared ceilings, and
the "Basis" column says which is which. Re-measure before relying on any of
them for a decision.

| Suite / spec                                | Wall clock   | Basis                                                   |
|---------------------------------------------+--------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| =npm test= (140 fixture tests)              | *≈ 65–75 s*  | measured twice, 2026-09-07 (66 s and 72 s)              |
| slowest single fixture spec                 | ≈ 60 s       | measured — =release-tracks-recording-length= (18 tests) |
| median individual fixture test              | ≈ 1.4 s      | measured                                                |
| slowest individual fixture test             | ≈ 9 s        | measured                                                |
| =npm run test:live= (=@core=, 10 tests)     | a few min    | estimate — mostly at the 120 s default                  |
| =artist-releases-filter-sort.spec.js=       | *≈ 7 m 45 s* | measured 2026-08-31, 11 tests, both opt-ins on          |
| =releasegroup-releases-filter-sort.spec.js= | ≈ 12 min+    | the spec's own note: ~2 min setup *per test* × 6        |
| =npm run test:live:extended= (64 tests)     | tens of min  | estimate; declared ceiling is 3 h 41 m                  |

The fixture suite's 66 s wall clock against ~327 s of summed test time is
parallelism doing its job across workers.

** Why some live specs take 8–15 minutes

The artwork specs dominate. A Cover Art Archive sweep over a 124-row release
group simply takes that long, so those specs raise their own timeouts and poll
until the painted-artwork count stops changing. Their settle budgets are
environment-tunable (all in ms):

| Variable               | Default | Used by                                    |
|------------------------+---------+--------------------------------------------|
| =SINGLE_CAA_SETTLE_MS= |  180000 | =caa-icon-survives-sort.spec.js=           |
| =MULTI_CAA_SETTLE_MS=  |  300000 | =caa-icon-survives-sort-multi.spec.js=     |
| =MERGED_CAA_SETTLE_MS= |  180000 | =merged-view-caa-search-sync.spec.js=      |
| =SAVE_ART_SETTLE_MS=   |  180000 | =save-to-disk-strips-live-artwork.spec.js= |

** Opt-in test groups (off by default)

| Variable                | Effect                                                                      |
|-------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| =TEST_PREFILTER_LOAD=1= | Adds the pre-filtered disk-load group — roughly doubles that spec's runtime |
| =TEST_COLVIS=1=         | Adds the column-visibility group                                            |
| =SAVE_HTML=1=           | Dumps each test's rendered HTML under =test-results/rendered-html/=         |

* Login

Some pageTypes only exist for a logged-in editor (=/edit/notes-received=,
=/user/*/edits=, open edits).

#+begin_src sh
npm run auth:login          # opens a browser, log in once
#+end_src

This writes =playwright/.auth/vzell.json=, which is *gitignored on purpose*: a
saved session cookie is as good as a password for musicbrainz.org. Never commit
it.

Without that file the live suite runs *logged out*. It does not fail — it
silently renders the logged-out version of those pages, which is a far more
confusing outcome than an error.

Sessions do expire. =tests/support/authState.js= detects that case and prints a
warning before the run rather than letting it pass silently:

#+begin_example
⚠  [chromium-live] Saved MusicBrainz session is NOT usable:
   "musicbrainz_server_session" expired …
   The run will continue LOGGED OUT.
   Fix: npm run auth:login
#+end_example

If you see that and the run still passes, the specs in it did not depend on
being logged in — but re-run =npm run auth:login= before capturing any snapshot
baseline, or it will diff against the logged-in one over header chrome alone.

* If a run seems to hang

*Check for a dialog waiting on a click before assuming a crash.* The userscript
has four gates that block until answered, and they are plain DOM overlays rather
than native browser dialogs, so nothing dismisses them automatically and no
console error appears.

| Gate                            | Fires when                                                   |
|---------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------|
| ℹ️ Unknown Page Count           | An edit-listing page whose pagination has no true last page  |
| ⚠️ High Page Count              | More pages than =sa_max_page= (default 50)                   |
| 💾 Save to Disk / 🎨 Render Now | More rows than =sa_render_threshold= (default 5000)          |
| ⚠️ Large Render Warning         | More rows than =sa_render_warning_threshold= (default 10000) |

The last two fire *after* the fetch finishes, so hitting one wastes the entire
fetch and then times out. Run with =npm run test:headed= to see which dialog is
up.

The fix is normally to seed the relevant setting so the dialog never appears —
=seedGmValues= in =tests/pagetypes.json= for snapshot captures,
=buildGmStubsScript(initialValues)= for fixture specs. *Seed a large number, not
zero*: =sa_render_threshold= reads =… || 5000=, so =0= is falsy and silently
becomes 5000 again, despite the setting's description promising "0 to disable".
=sa_render_warning_threshold= does honour =0=.

* Reading the results

- =npm run report= opens the last HTML report. It embeds per-test durations,
  traces for failures, and screenshots.
- =playwright-report/= and =test-results/= are both gitignored — treat them as
  this-run-only.
- Failures retain a trace (=trace: 'retain-on-failure'=) and a screenshot. Open
  the trace from the HTML report; it is usually faster than re-running.
- The two =test:live:report:*= scripts additionally generate a timestamped
  =.org= + =.html= filter/sort report under =debug/=, with a row per assertion
  case.
- Committed performance baselines live at
  =tests/snapshots/artist-events/interaction-perf-*.json= and
  =tests/snapshots/artist-releasegroups/perf-baseline*.json= — medians of 5
  samples, kept per branch.

* Where the maps are

| File                                        | What it tells you                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| =tests/live/registry.org=                   | Every live spec: pageType, URL, what it verifies, known quirks                                                        |
| =tests/snapshots/registry.org=              | Every snapshot baseline, plus an *"Expected drift"* section to read before treating a re-capture diff as a regression |
| =tests/pagetypes.json=                      | The 11 pageTypes wired into the snapshot harness, with their settings seeds                                           |
| =tests/MEASUREMENTS.org=                    | Every timing, wall clock and count measured, with the HOST it ran on                                                  |
| =PAGETYPES-TESTING-REFERENCE.org=           | Every pageType, a real URL for each, and the coverage plan                                                            |
| =tests/fixtures/live-userscripts/README.md= | The real-third-party-userscript interop harness                                                                       |

Note that =tests/snapshots/registry.org= lists more pageTypes than there are
directories on disk: baselines for personal-account pages are configured but not
committed.

* Directory layout

#+begin_example
tests/
  README.org          <- this file
  pagetypes.json      snapshot-harness config, read as data
  fixtures/           31 network-free specs + their saved HTML
    saved-data/       .json.gz Save-to-disk fixtures
    idb-state/        captured IndexedDB artwork records
    thirdPartyScripts/  hand-built third-party simulators
    live-userscripts/   real third-party bodies (gitignored) + manifest
  live/               37 real-page specs + registry.org
  snapshots/          per-pageType raw.html / rendered.html baselines
  support/            31 shared helpers, loaders, capture scripts
#+end_example

=tests/support/= holds the page loaders and GM_* stubs, the settle/assertion
helpers, the shared expected-value tables for the big filter/sort suites, and
the standalone capture scripts (=capture-snapshots.js=, =capture-fixture.js=,
=capture-interaction-perf.js=). Each has a JSDoc header explaining its own
non-obvious constraints; read that before working around one.

* Not a test: =npm run live-interop=

=tests/support/run-live-interop.js= opens a real MusicBrainz page with a chosen
combination of *real* third-party userscripts injected alongside this one, for
diagnosing interop problems by hand. It has *no pass/fail by design*, so a clean
run is not coverage of anything.

The userscript bodies it loads are gitignored — they are not ours to
redistribute — so only the harness and =manifest.json= are committed. Without
the bodies present the harness reports an empty set rather than failing.
